exactText: The way to the reconcile capability level of AI vs. GDP impact is that the diffusion of AI will take much longer than people think. ... AI diffusion is going to be the theme of the next decade.
sourceQuote: the diffusion of AI will take much longer than people think. ... AI diffusion is going to be the theme of the next decade.
normalizedClaim: AI capability will advance faster than its measurable GDP impact because diffusion through businesses will take much longer than expected, and diffusion will be the defining theme of the next decade.
resolutionCriteria: Comparison of AI capability benchmarks vs. macroeconomic productivity/GDP growth attributable to AI through 2035, as reported by OECD, BLS, or academic studies on technology diffusion.

exactText: in a world of 100X more AI agents than people in an enterprise, the value of the systems of record and tools agents will use will go up, not down.
sourceQuote: the value of the systems of record and tools agents will use will go up, not down.
normalizedClaim: In an enterprise environment with far more AI agents than humans, the value of systems of record and enterprise software tools will increase rather than decrease.
resolutionCriteria: Enterprise software market growth rates and valuation of systems-of-record vendors (e.g., Salesforce, SAP, Box, ServiceNow) relative to pure agent platforms through 2030, per Gartner or company financials.

exactText: Multi-model agentic systems clearly are the future.
sourceQuote: Multi-model agentic systems clearly are the future.
normalizedClaim: Multi-model agentic systems (frontier models as planners + cheaper models as workers) will become the dominant architecture for AI agents.
resolutionCriteria: Prevalence of multi-model orchestration in production agent frameworks from major providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, open-source) and enterprise deployments by 2029, documented in technical blogs and market reports.

exactText: We are so unbelievably early with agents right now. ... The same will happen for agents. ... This gives you a sense for how early we actually are in this transformation.
sourceQuote: We are so unbelievably early with agents right now.
normalizedClaim: Enterprise adoption of AI agents is still in a very early stage, analogous to cloud computing around 2010, with massive growth ahead.
resolutionCriteria: Growth in enterprise agent usage and revenue (comparable to cloud’s ~1000x expansion from 2010–2025) measured by 2035 via industry reports from Gartner, IDC, or hyperscaler earnings.

exactText: Jevons paradox is coming to knowledge work. By making it far cheaper to take on any type of task that we can possibly imagine, we’re ultimately going to be doing far more. The vast majority of AI tokens in the future will be used on things we don't even do today as workers
sourceQuote: Jevons paradox is coming to knowledge work.
normalizedClaim: Jevons paradox will apply to knowledge work: cheaper AI-driven tasks will lead to substantially more total work, with most future AI tokens spent on currently non-existent activities.
resolutionCriteria: Token consumption data and enterprise surveys showing majority of AI usage directed at novel workflows (new software projects, expanded reviews, additional research) rather than pure replacement of existing tasks by 2030.

exactText: AI productivity gains could lead to companies growing faster, causing them "to actually hire more people in either that function or other functions"
sourceQuote: to actually hire more people in either that function or other functions
normalizedClaim: AI-driven productivity gains will cause many companies to hire more people overall rather than simply reduce headcount.
resolutionCriteria: Labor market data (BLS occupational employment) and firm-level studies showing net employment growth in AI-adopting firms in knowledge-work sectors through 2030.

exactText: One sector that Levie predicts will grow in importance will be sales. ... The medical industry is another sector that Levie predicts will require more workers.
sourceQuote: sales. ... The medical industry is another sector that Levie predicts will require more workers.
normalizedClaim: Sales and healthcare will be among the sectors that experience job growth due to AI.
resolutionCriteria: BLS or equivalent occupational employment statistics showing net job growth in sales and healthcare occupations between 2025 and 2030 relative to overall employment trends.

exactText: The best opportunities right now are those where you can value to customers today with things that are barely only possible, but with a full mission that feels nearly impossible with today’s tech
sourceQuote: The best opportunities right now are those where you can value to customers today with things that are barely only possible, but with a full mission that feels nearly impossible with today’s tech
normalizedClaim: The strongest AI product opportunities are those that deliver value with currently marginal capabilities while targeting missions that become feasible only with future orders-of-magnitude improvements.
resolutionCriteria: Success rates and valuation outcomes of AI startups that launched with “barely possible” features in 2026 and scaled with subsequent capability gains, tracked through 2030 venture and public-market data.

exactText: Frontier intelligence continues unabated and pushes the industry forward continuously. ... Open weights rapidly absorbs frontier breakthroughs ... The Applied AI layer has a huge opportunity to combine frontier intelligence with open or cheap closed models
sourceQuote: Frontier intelligence continues unabated and pushes the industry forward continuously.
normalizedClaim: Frontier AI progress will continue without plateau, open-weight models will rapidly absorb those advances, and applied AI orchestration layers will thrive by combining both.
resolutionCriteria: Continued release of significantly stronger frontier models alongside rapid open-weight equivalents, plus growth of multi-model applied platforms, observable through 2029 model releases and market reports.

exactText: The race to create the best AI model over the next five years is "anybody's game"
sourceQuote: The race to create the best AI model over the next five years is "anybody's game"
normalizedClaim: No single lab is locked in as the permanent leader in frontier AI models over the next five years (through ~2030); leadership remains contestable.
resolutionCriteria: Changes in relative leadership on major benchmarks and enterprise adoption among OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI, and others between 2025 and 2030.
